label: Cut-up line (wing separation)
description: The first and most important mixing point. Wings are cut from the carcass and drop onto a shared conveyor. A bird's left and right wing part company here and, in a commodity plant, never meet again.

label: Wing chiller
description: Bulk immersion or air chilling. Thousands of wings tumble together in a single vessel with a residence time measured in tens of minutes.

label: Size grading (jumbo / large / medium)
description: Wings are weighed individually and routed to grade streams. This is ACTIVE SEPARATION, not shuffling: a bird's two wings go to different boxes whenever they fall on opposite sides of a grade boundary. The single strongest driver pushing the answer toward 12.

label: Combo bin
description: Bulk container, commonly around 2,000 lb. At roughly 0.23 lb per whole wing that is about 8,700 wings in one bin.

label: IQF freezer tunnel
description: Individually quick frozen on a continuous belt. Continuous flow means no lot boundaries are preserved through this step.

label: Case pack
description: Boxed, commonly 40 lb - roughly 175 wings. Packing does not mix; it draws from an already-mixed stream. By this point essentially every wing in the case is from a different bird.

label: Distributor warehouse
description: Pallets assembled from many lots, plants, and sometimes producers.

label: Restaurant freezer bin
description: The bin is topped up from multiple cases across multiple deliveries. Old and new stock commingle - the practical reason a single order can span weeks of production.

label: Fryer basket
description: The draw itself. Twelve wings are scooped from the bin - the point at which the question finally gets answered.
